bio.headline: About.
bio.story: I'm Juan Sebastian Acosta Pinilla, a Colombo-Canadian full-stack dev living in Montréal, Quebec. I love turning wild ideas into real web apps—think slick React frontends, solid Django backends, or e-commerce sites with Stripe that just work. Coming from sound design and cooking gigs, I've got that knack for precision and adapting on the fly, now channeling it into code.

personality.headline: My Vibe and Style
personality.story: I’m an iterative problem-solver and detail-oriented team player, at home in structured workflows like GitHub Issues, Milestones, Kanban boards (Trello/Jira), and Figma collaboration. Frequent commits, rebasing, and early CI/CD setup ensure clean, reliable code and smooth team integration.

background.headline: My Journey So Far
background.story: I began with electroacoustic composition at Universidad Tres de Febrero (Argentina), sound design at Tecson Studio(Argentina), and culinary roles—including sous chef at Taco Club (Revelstoke, BC) and service at Hotel Alvear Palace (Argentina). After obtaining Canadian Permanent Residency, I pursued web development through Vanier College’s Web Design Specialist program, transforming high-pressure skills into full-stack capabilities.

key_projects.headline: Projects I'm Proud Of
key_projects.story: These projects highlight practical problem-solving for junior roles.

core_skills.headline: Skills in My Toolbox
databases: learning more about PostgreSQL and MongoDB.

development_process.headline: Development Process
development_process.story: I start with Figma ideation and requirements, organize via GitHub Projects/Issues or Trello/Jira, then iterate with branching/commits, CI/CD, component/unit tests, and deployment (GitHub Pages currently; Vercel/Netlify next). This agile approach delivers quality code efficiently.

influences.headline: What Fires Me Up
influences.story: I love reading books on programming and design, with “The Pragmatic Programmer” by Andrew Hunt and David Thomas standing out as a key influence—its emphasis on clean, modular code shapes my approach. This aligns with Svelte’s unified components, Python’s versatility across ML, data, and servers, and FastAPI’s elegant simplicity. Mentors Maxime Pigeon and Marc-André Charpentier, UX principles from Nielsen/Norman (via Interaction Design Foundation), and Linus Torvalds’ pragmatic style further keep me user-focused and efficient.

career_goals.headline: Where I'm Headed
career_goals.story: Right now? Land a Montréal backend internship where I can learn fast. Mid-term: Rack up real projects, crush databases and queries, pick up a new language yearly (Go in 2026!). Long-term: Lead projects, dip into open-source part-time. This career switch has me excited for whatever comes next.
